H: the first letter of the two-letter alphabet used in the counting proof
T: the second letter of the two-letter alphabet used in the counting proof
A_k: the set of binary strings of length 2k+1 containing at least k+1 ones
j: the integer indexing the position k+j+1 of the (k+1)-st one in the binary-word partition
\\mathcal A: The set of length-(2k+1) words over {H,T} containing at least k+1 occurrences of H.
\\mathcal B: The set of length-(2k+1) words over {H,T} containing at least k+1 occurrences of T.
\\mathcal A_j: For 0<=j<=k, the subset of \mathcal A whose (k+1)-st H occurs in position k+j+1.
binary word: A finite sequence all of whose entries are in the two-element set {0,1}.
A_j: For fixed k and 0<=j<=k, the set of binary words of length 2k+1 whose (k+1)-st zero occurs at position k+j+1.
Z_k: The set of binary words of length 2k+1 containing at least k+1 zeros.
O_k: The set of binary words of length 2k+1 containing at least k+1 ones.
\\(\\mathcal{B}_k\\): For a fixed nonnegative integer k, the set of binary words of length 2k+1 having at least k+1 entries equal to 1.
\\(\\mathcal{B}_{k,j}\\): For integers k and j with k nonnegative and 0<=j<=k, the subset of B_k whose (k+1)-st entry equal to 1 is preceded by exactly j entries equal to 0.
\\mathcal W: the set of length-(2k+1) words over {H,T} having strictly more H occurrences than T occurrences
